trials.content:
FIFO stands for **First-In, First-Out**. 

In the context of a queue, it means that the first element added to the structure is the first one to be removed. You can think of it like a line at a coffee shop: the person who gets in line first is the first one served.

sample.question: What is the ordering principle of a queue?
sample.answer: A queue follows first in, first out (FIFO) ordering.
sample.sourceQuote: A queue follows first in, first out (FIFO) ordering.

sample.question: How does a stack differ from a queue in terms of ordering?
sample.answer: A stack follows last in, first out (LIFO) ordering, whereas a queue follows FIFO.
sample.sourceQuote: A stack instead follows last in, first out (LIFO) ordering.

sample.question: What happens when an enqueue operation is attempted on a full Aster queue?
sample.answer: The enqueue operation rejects the new item and preserves all existing items.
sample.sourceQuote: When the Aster queue is full, enqueue rejects the new item and preserves all existing items.
